entities.summary:
The Armenian Democratic Liberal Party (ADL, Armenian: Ռամկավար Ազատական Կուսակցություն, Ramkavar Azatakan Kusaktsutyun), founded in 1921 through the merger of the Armenian Constitutional Democratic Party (Sahmanadrutyun) and the Armenian Democratic Liberal Party — is one of the three traditional Armenian diaspora political parties (alongside the Armenian Revolutionary Federation/Dashnaks and the Hunchakian Party), representing the liberal democratic strand of Armenian diaspora politics across North America, Europe, and the Middle East.

The three traditional Armenian political parties were founded in the late 19th and early 20th centuries to advocate for Armenian rights in the Ottoman Empire and to mobilize the Armenian diaspora communities created by the Armenian Genocide (1915-1923). The ARF (Dashnak) represents a more nationalist and sometimes socialist position; the Hunchakian Party originated as a socialist organization; and the Ramkavar (ADL) has historically taken a more liberal democratic and diaspora-focused position.

The ADL's political positions have been shaped by its diaspora orientation: unlike the ARF, which historically had ambivalent positions on the Soviet Armenian Republic, the ADL was more willing to cooperate with Soviet Armenia (and the Soviet-era Armenian SSR government) as a pragmatic means of preserving Armenian culture and connections. After Armenian independence (1991), the ADL has been active in Armenia's political sphere though remaining primarily a diaspora institution. The ADL publishes the Armenian Mirror-Spectator (Boston), one of the oldest Armenian-American newspapers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Armenian Democratic Liberal Party — one of three traditional Armenian diaspora parties sustaining political and cultural life for Armenian Genocide survivors and their descendants for over a century — is historically significant as an institution of Armenian diaspora resilience and political organization.
